Export or share and any delivery completion are separately receipted and never inferred from authorization. Stage 30 closes through the one atomic CALCULATE_TERMINAL command, which reads the precondition revision, validates registry integrity and all terminal prerequisites, creates exactly one current terminal determination, sets DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED only when every prerequisite is true and otherwise BLOCKED, increments revision once, and commits once. The command's own committed revision does not invalidate its result; only a later revision affecting its dependency closure may supersede or withdraw it. Registry incompleteness blocks Stage 30 unless it proves an earlier premise false; it does not create a Stage 27↔Stage 30 cycle.

decisions.priorControllingText: Because the canonical handoff container is logical under Section 19.7, per-member sequential export or share on the pinned device satisfies package export whenever a combined multi-file share is unavailable; the optional archive representation is never required. Before the acceptance run, the acceptance procedure executes a recorded MOBILE_CAPABILITY_PROBE on the pinned target covering file export or share, response-file selection, returned-file slot selection, persistent-storage request, logical package export, and backup export and restore. A required capability the pinned target cannot perform yields BLOCKED with the exact missing capability recorded. The only permitted continuations are a new pinned target record on an iOS or Safari version that supports the capability, or a governance change to the controlling specification. No silent degradation path exists.

decisions.priorControllingText: The evidence file reaches CI through the repository as a committed file or authenticated workflow input from a submitter recorded in the acceptance artifact. Each MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CHALLENGE is single-use: CI accepts at most one evidence file per challenge and rejects reused, unknown, or expired challenges and any evidence bound to a different commit, manifest, origin, target, or test project; a superseding run requires a new challenge. The gate minimum for the physical-device fact is HUMAN_OBSERVATION by the recorded performer at the recorded identity assurance; that basis is explicitly sufficient and is never relabeled application-proven.

decisions.priorControllingText: Before deployment, CI creates closed-loop-deployment-manifest/1 from the audited source commit. It lists canonical origin/base path, source commit, workflow run, build identity, canonicalization and registry identities, build command/environment, workflow-file digest, dependency/lockfile identities, CSP value, and every runtime HTML, JavaScript, CSS, worker, icon, manifest, schema, and asset path with media type, byte length, hash algorithm, and digest. The deployment manifest carries one overall manifest digest computed under closed-loop-canonical-json/1 with the digest field itself omitted; no manifest digest includes itself. Unmanifested runtime resources are prohibited.

decisions.priorControllingText: The application has no controlling service worker unless it is explicitly required, manifested, versioned, security-reviewed, and tested. Clean-profile and previously cached-profile acceptance must load one unmixed build identity or visibly block as stale. The running page, every script and style, and test-worker.js report or are bound to the expected build. Post-deployment verification retrieves every manifest path with cache bypass where supported and rejects missing, extra, redirected-to-different-content, cross-origin, stale, or modified resources. Browser acceptance proves the executed HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and worker resource graph matches the same manifest and build identity; mixed or stale cached builds fail.
